description: Verification of the persistent external scorer protocol in run_experiment.py. The persistent protocol eliminates process-spawn overhead by keeping the scorer process alive for all fixture cases. Measured mock latencies demonstrate the overhead difference between per-case subprocess and persistent pipe-based communication.

protocols_tested.name: builtin-mock
protocols_tested.description: Built-in no-op mock. No subprocess overhead.

protocols_tested.name: subprocess-per-case-mock
protocols_tested.description: External mock scorer invoked as subprocess per case.

protocols_tested.name: persistent-mock
protocols_tested.description: External mock scorer started once, communicated via stdin/stdout pipes.

builtin_mock.note: No-op in-process mock; latency is sub-microsecond.

subprocess_per_case_mock.note: Subprocess spawn dominates; Python interpreter startup is ~13-20ms per case.

persistent_mock.note: Persistent pipe communication; sub-50us steady-state. First case at 12.9ms (Python warmup anomaly).

latency_reduction.description: Persistent mock p95 (45us) is ~430x faster than per-case subprocess mock p95 (19,380us).

capabilities_verified: Persistent scorer process startup and lifecycle management
Per-case JSON line write to stdin with flush
Per-case JSON line read from stdout with select-based timeout
Fallback detection: timeout, broken pipe, persistent_exit
Process death recovery: remaining cases marked as persistent_process_died
Mock scorer persistent mode: reads JSONL from stdin until EOF
Mock scorer persistent + oracle mode compatibility
Privacy: per-case output remains sanitized (no scorer output, readings, candidates, expected, or baseline text)
remaining_risks: select(2) is Unix-only; Windows would need asyncio or threading.Timer fallback
Stderr pipe can fill and block the scorer process if verbose logging is enabled during benchmark loop
First-case latency anomaly (12.9ms vs 31us steady-state) not fully characterized; may be Python JIT warmup or process scheduler jitter
Real model wrappers may have different latency profiles and failure modes than the mock
No built-in mechanism to restart a dead persistent process mid-run; all remaining cases become fallback
conclusion: Persistent scorer protocol verified. The persistent mock eliminates process-spawn overhead (~430x at p95), reducing communication latency from 19ms to 45us. This makes it feasible to benchmark tiny LLM wrappers under the Phase 2 latency budget (p95 < 20ms commit-time reranking) without the measurement being swamped by subprocess overhead. The select(2)-based timeout works correctly on Linux. The implementation is ready for real model wrapper integration.
